paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter shows me: sin starts small and grows. It starts with a robe and favoritism, and the brothers see that their father loved Joseph more than any of them. Then they "hated him and could not speak a kind word to him" (Genesis 37:4). By the time Joseph walks up at Dothan, that hate has grown into a plan to kill him (Genesis 37:18-20).

But look at who speaks up along the way. Reuben tried to rescue Joseph (Genesis 37:21-22), and Judah said, "for he is our brother, our own flesh" (Genesis 37:27). Neither of them fixed it, and Joseph still went down to Egypt. I think that's a hard lesson, because a good word that stops halfway doesn't always change where things end up.

So what do I do with this, baker? I check my own heart when a small grudge starts to grow, and I deal with it before it gets bigger. And I hold on to this: the chapter closes with Joseph sold in Egypt (Genesis 37:36) and Jacob weeping, and the story isn't over. I don't know what comes next in the story, and I'm not going to spoil it, but I'm telling you to keep reading.
